name: Septorhinoplasty

card.summary: Combined surgery on the nasal septum and the outer nose, done for breathing and shape together; the evidence base is mostly surgical case series, with recovery details well documented.
card.note: Surgical procedure under anaesthesia; swelling and tip position can take months to a year to settle, and revision surgery is a documented possibility.

quick.overview:
Septorhinoplasty combines septoplasty (straightening the cartilage and bone wall inside the nose) with rhinoplasty (reshaping the outside of the nose). It is performed when a person has both a breathing problem from a deviated septum and a wish to change nasal appearance, such as a crooked bridge after a past injury.

On looksmaxxing forums it appears in threads where members ask whether they need a plain rhinoplasty or the combined operation, and in recovery threads about swelling and tip position. Published research on it is largely surgical series and trials of peri-operative care rather than comparisons of cosmetic outcomes.
quick.mechanism: The surgeon works on the septum to correct deviation and on the nasal cartilages and bones to alter the external shape, using an open or closed approach. Cartilage from the septum is often reused as graft material, and the nasal bones may be repositioned.
quick.risks: Documented issues include bruising and swelling, persisting obstruction (sometimes linked to enlarged turbinates), the need for revision surgery, and anaesthesia-related effects such as sore throat. It is a prescription-level surgical procedure performed by licensed surgeons; outcomes vary by surgeon and anatomy.

lead: Septorhinoplasty is an operation that combines septoplasty, which straightens a deviated nasal septum, with rhinoplasty, which reshapes the external nose. It is used when a person has both an obstructed airway and an aesthetic concern, for example a crooked nose following an old injury [1][2]. People who choose it are usually after a straighter bridge, a better-proportioned profile or a refined tip, together with easier nasal breathing, and the nose sits at the centre of the face, so changes to it alter how the whole face reads in photographs and in profile [12][29].

Surgeons describe it as a common functional-aesthetic procedure, and trials registered in several countries study its recovery, pain control and outcomes [3][4]. The published evidence mostly consists of technique reports, retrospective reviews and randomised trials of adjuncts such as tranexamic acid, corticosteroids, analgesia and anaesthetic methods, rather than head-to-head tests of aesthetic results [5][6][7]. A 1992 review of septal surgery noted that, although its benefit seems intuitive, relatively few papers had confirmed it when the review was written; a later randomised trial, summarised by Wikipedia, found septoplasty improved symptoms and quality of life at six months more than nasal sprays did [8][26].

In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed mainly by people deciding between a rhinoplasty alone and the combined operation, by people asking how it fits around orthodontic treatment, and by people describing post-operative swelling and tip rotation [9][10]. Rhinoplasty more broadly has been a major topic on social media, where a 2020 to 2021 TikTok trend under the label nose job check drew over a billion views for the hashtag [12].

chain: Surgeon straightens the septum and reshapes the bones, cartilage and tip
Nose is straighter, better proportioned and easier to breathe through
Face looks more balanced in profile and front-on
angle.text: Septorhinoplasty is used to correct a crooked or deviated nose and to change its shape in one operation, so the airway and the outer contour are addressed together. Results settle over the following year as swelling resolves [12][26].

paras: The septum is the cartilage-and-bone partition that divides the nasal cavity. When it is deviated, the airway on one side can be narrowed. Wikipedia reports that some septal displacement is present in about 80 percent of people, usually unnoticed, and that unequal growth, birth trauma, later facial blows from sport or accidents and connective tissue disorders are among the causes [27]. Septoplasty straightens or removes the deviated portions; rhinoplasty alters the shape of the nasal bones, cartilages and tip. In septorhinoplasty both are done in one session [1][11].

The American Society of Plastic Surgeons describes rhinoplasty as changing the size or proportions of the nose to improve facial harmony and as able to correct breathing problems from structural defects, with a deviated septum named as one of the most common causes of impaired breathing. Its list of aesthetic targets includes nose size relative to the face, bridge width, humps or depressions, tip shape, nostril size and asymmetry [29].

Wikipedia's rhinoplasty article describes surgeons analysing the nose against proportions such as a nasofrontal angle of 115 to 130 degrees, a nasolabial angle of about 90 to 95 degrees in men and 100 to 105 in women, and a nose of about one third of facial height, along with nine aesthetic subunits that guide incisions and repair [12].

Surgeons may use the external (open) approach, which adds a columellar incision and gives a better view and tip precision, or the endonasal (closed) approach with all incisions inside the nose, which typically involves less dissection and faster recovery. Open surgery is usually preferred for revision cases [12]. A general rhinoplasty reference notes that systematic reviews have not found significant long-term differences in functional or aesthetic scores between open and closed approaches [12]. A review of the internal technique describes it as the standard operation until the open approach became popular, and argues that both have indications [35].

Technique reports describe methods for lower-third nasal work, such as the tongue-in-groove technique, which a 10-year experience paper presents as a way to correct excess columellar show and maintain correction of caudal deviation while controlling tip rotation and projection [13]. Septal cartilage composition has also been studied because the septum is a common graft source [14]. Septal grafts are the usual material for reshaping and support, with ear or rib cartilage used when septal cartilage is insufficient [12].

A review of septal extension grafts in Asian rhinoplasty describes the graft as a way to control tip projection, shape and rotation and notes complications such as a foreshortened nose from earlier implants [34]. Other reports cover reusing a bone-cartilaginous unit in revision rhinoplasty, a technique called septorhinoplasty by disarticulation, and repair of septal perforations through the external approach [40][42][15].

Nose repair is among the oldest recorded operations: the Edwin Smith Papyrus (about 3000 to 2500 BCE) mentions repair of a broken nose, and the text of Sushruta in ancient India describes rebuilding a nose with a cheek flap. Gasparo Tagliacozzi published a manual in 1597 describing nasal reconstruction with an arm flap [12].

Modern cosmetic and functional work took shape from the late 1800s. John Orlando Roe performed the first modern endonasal rhinoplasty in 1887 to treat a saddle nose, Freer and Killian pioneered submucous resection of the septum in 1902 and 1904, and Jacques Joseph described nose reduction through internal incisions in 1928. Aurel Rethi introduced the open approach in 1934, Maurice Cottle's 1947 hemitransfixion approach to septal deviation helped make closed surgery the standard, and the open approach was popularised from the 1970s by Padovan and Wilfred Goodman and extended to revision surgery by Jack Gunter in 1987 [12].

By the 1980s reports described closing septal perforations through the external septorhinoplasty approach, and papers in the 1990s and 2000s analysed specific techniques and the properties of septal cartilage [15][13][14].

Evaluation includes history, examination, photographs from several angles and an assessment of the patient's motivation; tests such as the Cottle manoeuvre check for internal valve collapse, which spreader grafts may correct [12]. Septoplasty is generally not done during an acute nasal or sinus infection, and is avoided in people with untreated diabetes, severe hypertension or bleeding disorders, according to Wikipedia [26].

Planning questions on forums often concern whether a crooked nose after an adolescent injury needs the combined operation and how orthodontic work should be timed; the published sources cited here do not address the sequencing of braces and nose surgery [9]. In children, reviews describe a cautious approach because surgery can disturb growth zones: treatment of nasal and septal fractures is often closed reduction and splinting at the time, with open septorhinoplasty at skeletal maturity if needed, and cleft nasal deformities are ideally addressed near the end of nasal growth [31][32][33][30].

Septoplasty is performed through the nostrils with an incision in the septal lining, and may use small internal splints for about 7 to 10 days; most operations take about an hour or less, and bleeding is a risk for up to two weeks, affecting about 1 percent of patients, per Wikipedia [26]. After rhinoplasty, patients typically convalesce for about a week, external sutures come out at 4 to 5 days, the external cast at about a week, and periorbital bruising settles by about two weeks; tissues continue to shift over the first year [12].

Swelling after rhinoplasty can take at least a year to fully resolve, according to a general rhinoplasty reference [12]. Nasal tissues mostly settle within three to six months after septoplasty, with shifting possible for more than a year [26]. Forum members describe a tip that sits very high in the first days and then drops, with reported times ranging from about a week to six months or more [10].

A review of inferior turbinate hypertrophy notes that nasal obstruction can persist after a technically sound septorhinoplasty if enlarged turbinates are not addressed, and that management of turbinate hypertrophy has been debated for over a century [16]. Registered trials have compared septorhinoplasty with and without turbinate surgery for such patients [17][18]. A registered study examined the effect of septorhinoplasty on allergic rhinitis [23].

A randomised study in septorhinoplasty patients examined tranexamic acid and corticosteroid for post-operative swelling and bruising [7]. A double-blind trial of 198 septorhinoplasty candidates randomised patients to topical tranexamic acid or control to assess surgical-field bleeding [37]. Other trials in patients undergoing septorhinoplasty have tested a ketamine gargle for post-operative sore throat after intubation, nitrous oxide for opioid-induced hyperalgesia after remifentanil-propofol anaesthesia, a single preventive intravenous dose of ketorolac and paracetamol for pain, and bilateral sphenopalatine ganglion block [5][6][38][41]. A randomised trial tested brochure-assisted education before surgery for its effect on fear and anxiety [39]. A review addressed the evidence for peri-operative antibiotics in otolaryngology [19].

Registered trials are examining nerve blocks, liposomal bupivacaine, fibrin glue and pain-score courses after the operation [20][21][22][4]. Wikipedia notes that a single dose of corticosteroids may reduce swelling and bleeding in the first two days with limited evidence, and that fat grafting may speed resolution of swelling and bruising [12].

Rhinoplasty is generally described as safe, but post-operative deformities are the main risk. Wikipedia lists pollybeak (excess fullness above the tip, said to account for about half of revisions), saddle nose from over-resection of the septal support, inverted-V collapse, rocker deformity, open roof deformity, an over-rotated tip, pinched tip and temporary columellar numbness; bleeding is uncommon and infection rare [12]. Septoplasty complications include a dropped nasal tip, septal perforation, septal hematoma or abscess, adhesions, numbness of the upper front teeth and reduced sense of smell [26].

A septal perforation, a hole through the septum, can follow nasal surgery. Small ones can whistle on breathing and larger ones may cause crusting, bleeding and breathing difficulty; options include observation, humidification, a silicone septal button or surgical closure [28]. A randomised comparison of burr-assisted septorhinoplasty with septoplasty alone examined hearing function in 40 patients [36]. A 2022 case report examined the cost-effectiveness of septorhinoplasty [43].

A study of cosmetic rhinoplasty at a plastic surgery group practice examined revision rates and risk factors for dissatisfaction and complications [24]. General references put the share of primary rhinoplasties needing further surgery at 5 to 20 percent [12]. Revision surgery often uses the open approach and cartilage grafts from the septum, ear or rib [12][40].

On looksmax.org the topic appears as planning questions (which operation to book, how it interacts with orthodontics, how to brief a surgeon on keeping the tip from rotating upward) and post-operative recovery reports [9][10]. Posters often describe an adolescent injury leading to a crooked bridge in later years and weigh a consultation fee against getting a clear plan from one surgeon [9].

Wider social-media attention to nose surgery includes the 2020 to 2021 nose job check TikTok trend, in which the sound was used in over 120,000 videos and the hashtag passed a billion views, as reported in Wikipedia's rhinoplasty article [12]. Non-surgical rhinoplasty with injectable fillers is an alternative that reshapes the nose without changing its size; it was preceded by early attempts using paraffin and silicone that proved harmful [12].

Human studies of septorhinoplasty include: a retrospective multi-hospital review of septal surgery efficacy (which excluded septorhinoplasty but frames the evidence for septal work) [8]; a 10-year series on the tongue-in-groove technique [13]; randomised trials of tranexamic acid and corticosteroid on swelling and bruising [7], topical tranexamic acid on bleeding [37], ketamine gargle for sore throat [5], nitrous oxide for hyperalgesia [6], ketorolac and paracetamol for pain [38], sphenopalatine ganglion block [41] and preoperative brochure education [39]; and registered trials covering allergic rhinitis outcomes, turbinate surgery quality of life, pain management and a 750-patient outcome analysis [23][18][17][20][21][3].

For septoplasty alone, a 2023 randomised trial reported greater symptom and quality-of-life improvement at six months than with nasal sprays [26]. Most trials of septorhinoplasty focus on peri-operative issues or functional measures; long-term aesthetic comparison data are limited.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the topic appears as planning questions (which operation to book, how it interacts with orthodontics) and post-operative recovery reports [9][10].

claims.claim: A crooked nose with a slightly deviated septum calls for septorhinoplasty rather than rhinoplasty alone.
claims.believers: A poster in a planning thread reasons that a plain rhinoplasty would leave the deviated septum, which could affect the nose again, and asks whether the combined operation is the better choice.[9]
claims.experts: Surgical literature describes septorhinoplasty as the combined operation for septal deviation with external deformity.[1][2] Individual recommendations depend on examination, and no source reviewed provides a general rule.

claims.claim: Braces or aligners should be timed relative to nose surgery because they could put pressure on the nose.
claims.believers: The same poster says they have read that braces can put pressure on the nose and asks whether orthodontics should come first.[9]
claims.experts: No study in the reviewed sources examines the sequencing of orthodontic treatment and septorhinoplasty.

claims.claim: A very upturned tip right after surgery is normal and drops over time.
claims.believers: Members who have had the surgery say the tip drops back, with reported times ranging from about a week to six months or more.[10]
claims.experts: A general rhinoplasty reference states that swelling can take at least a year to resolve.[12] No study in the reviewed sources quantifies tip rotation change.

claims.claim: Telling the surgeon repeatedly not to make the nose upturned gives a natural, straight result.
claims.believers: One member reports being happy with a natural-looking, straight outcome after repeating this instruction and choosing a good surgeon.[9]
claims.experts: Surgical series describe techniques for controlling tip rotation and projection.[13] Patient satisfaction after nasal surgery varies; revision rates are documented.[24]

claims.claim: A nose that became crooked after a teenage injury can be corrected with surgery in adulthood.
claims.believers: An 18-year-old poster describes a bridge that was symmetrical until an injury around age 14 or 15 and has become crooked with age, and plans surgery with a well-regarded surgeon [9].
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists facial blows from sport or accidents among the causes of septal deviation, and the rhinoplasty literature describes functional-aesthetic surgery for post-traumatic deformity [27][12]. Reviews of paediatric surgery describe waiting until skeletal maturity for open septorhinoplasty in many cases [31].
